title: The Chinese Teapot That Gets Better Every Year | China Travel Expert
description:
Most teapots are just teapots. A Yixing zisha (purple-clay) pot is the rare one that improves the more you brew in it.

The secret is the clay: a mineral-rich "purple sand" found around Yixing in Jiangsu — and almost nowhere else. Potters there have worked it for roughly 600 years, since the Ming dynasty, and they leave it unglazed on purpose. The raw, porous surface slowly drinks in the oils of the tea you brew, so over years the pot "seasons" and gives each cup a rounder, richer, softer taste. That's also why you never scrub a good zisha pot with soap. The craft is listed as one of China's national intangible cultural heritages.

🧭 Expert Tip: If you want a real one, buy in Yixing/Dingshu, match the pot to one tea type, and rinse with hot water only — never soap.
